texts.facts: The deceased girl was treated cruelly by the accused during her lifetime before the incident. On the letter, the Doctor had accepted the fact that the Medical Panel is of the opinion that the injuries on the private parts of the body of the deceased girl and the broken neck bone was a result of a sexual crime and the girl's neck was hit while committing sexual crime. By applying excessive pressure so that the child does not cry, it was possible for the child's throat cartilage and trachea to break. In this way, the accused raped and murdered the one and a half year old deceased girl. 23. The accused has been convicted for the offences under Sections 376 (2) & 302 of IPC and Section 5(e) read with Section 6 and Section 5(n) read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act. 24. Since there was no evidence on the file that the accused had destroyed the body of the deceased girl in order to save himself from the crime of rape and murder of the deceased girl, hence, he was acquitted of the offence under Section 201 of IPC. State Of Uttarakhand vs Yusuf Alias Sonu on 2 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72640915/ 9 25. As far as awarding sentence to the accused is concerned, the Trial Court had referred to the judgments of the Supreme Court in Bachan Singh vs. State of Punjab, AIR 1980 SC 898; Kehar Singh vs. State (Delhi Administration) AIR 1988 SC 1883; Swami Shraddhanand alias Murli Manohar Mishra (2) vs. State of Karnataka, (2008) 13 SCC 767; Shankar Krishna Rav vs. State of Maharashtra, 2013 (5) SCC 546; and Mukesh and others vs. State of NCT Delhi and others, Criminal Appeal No. 607-608/2017 AIR 2017 SC 2061. 26. Thereafter, in the meantime, on 09.03.2011 in Writ Petition No. 52 of 2011, preferred by the accused- appellant, Supreme Court granted stay of execution of death sentence.
